summary.text: A boy, born at term to a mother already on antiretroviral therapy, had an uneventful neonatal period, a culture-negative sepsis admission at 3 months, and an admission at 8 months with two weeks of abdominal distention and vomiting. Examination showed mild scleral icterus, a distended soft abdomen and irregular nontender 6 cm hepatomegaly; renal tests were read as consistent with dehydration, cultures were negative and the chest X-ray was unremarkable.

Ultrasound and MRI showed hepatomegaly and a left-lobe liver lesion consistent with hemangioma, and propranolol was started. Serial ultrasounds from age 1 to 4 years showed the liver mass unchanged, and weight stayed above 0 Z-score.

At 4 years he was cyanosed with clubbing, chemosis, hepatosplenomegaly and low oxygen saturation, with polycythemia and thrombocytopenia. Hepatopulmonary syndrome and portal hypertension were suspected; CT in South Africa showed a left-lobe mass suggestive of hemangioma and splenomegaly, and echocardiography with a saline bubble test showed a structurally normal heart with a positive bubble test.

Exploration found no mass but advanced cirrhosis, and wedge biopsy showed distorted architecture with regenerative nodules and fibrosis, with Wilson disease, alpha-1 antitrypsin disease and metabolic disease excluded. He was assessed as having cryptogenic cirrhosis and severe hepatopulmonary syndrome, put on home oxygen and advised to return for transplant work-up, but could not return for financial reasons and died on home oxygen; autopsy was declined.

Supplement f1 is a DOCX of scanned histopathology and cardiology reports (images only); its printed values are pixel content reviewed in the supplement sidecar, not copied into the article facts or used as conflict sides.
Table 1 value cells carry no units; units and reference intervals are copied from the row labels as printed and no high/low flags were assigned from them. Dash cells are missing values, not zeros.
Text statements about the 8-month and 4-year laboratory findings are kept separate from Table 1 cells because the source does not tie them to the same measurements.
The case describes the 8-month admission, the MRI "3 months later", propranolol and later ultrasound scans without calendar dates; only stated ages and intervals are recorded.
Discussion paragraphs mostly cite literature; only sentences that say "our patient/child" were used as index-patient facts.
Echocardiography, exploration and wedge biopsy are not ordered against each other or against the CT; the timeline after the 4-year presentation is only partly ordered.
